Purchase-order finance

After this lesson you can:
  • Fund production before a receivable exists
  • Control milestones from order to settlement

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

1. The product

One step earlier than invoice discounting: the seller holds a confirmed purchase order but needs working capital to produce and ship. The lender funds against the order's value and cost estimate, releasing money at fulfilment milestones — raw material, production, shipment — and recovers from the buyer's payment after delivery.

Risk is double: performance risk (will the seller deliver?)

stacks on buyer credit risk.

Margins between order value and cost, incoterms and shipment evidence are contract facts because they are the risk math.

2. What a BA watches

Milestone drawdown discipline is everything — funding ahead of verified progress converts trade finance into an unsecured loan to a hopeful manufacturer. Buyer-cancellation management is the designed answer to the order evaporating mid-production.

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. What extra risk does PO finance carry over invoice discounting?

  1. None
  2. Performance risk — the goods do not exist yet, so the seller must first deliver
  3. Currency risk only
  4. Lower margins
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. An invoice evidences completed delivery; a purchase order only promises it — milestone controls manage that gap.
